beats.text: Nobody wrote that it hit him.
beats.note: In the passages read, Newton's story is of an apple falling while he sat thinking, not of a blow to the head.

beats.text: It comes from his friend William Stukeley.
beats.note: Stukeley's account describes tea in the garden under apple trees, and Newton saying the idea was occasioned by the fall of an apple, as he sat in contemplative mood.

beats.name: A spring afternoon
beats.role: When, according to the Associated Press, Newton shared the story with Stukeley over tea.

beats.note: Physics World says he appears to have repeated the story often in later life, but never wrote it down.

beats.name: Stukeley's biography
beats.role: The year the account was first published, long after the 1660s plague retreat it describes.

beats.name: The Royal Society
beats.role: Put the handwritten manuscript online, with the apple story on pages 42 and 43.

beats.text: The apple stays. The bump on the head goes.
